newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: CANTV says Movilnet unit gets $75 mln IFC loan.
newsitem.headline: CANTV says Movilnet unit gets $75 mln IFC loan.

text.p: Venezuelan national telephone company CANTV said its mobile telephone subsidiary Movilnet had received two loans from the International Finance Corporation (IFC) worth a total of $75 million.
CANTV executive vice president Andres Gluski said in a release that the two loans had a grace period to January 2000.
One loan for $35 million directly from the IFC, has a maturity 10 years and an interest rate of two percent above the six-month Libor rate.
The second loan, for $40 million coordinated by the IFC on behalf of a group of commercial banks, has a maturity of eight years and an interest rate of 1.75 percent above the six-month Libor rate.
Movilnet President Guillermo Olaizola said the loans would go toward the company's $178.4 million investment program to expand its coverage and improve technology.
